attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps both halves and the 'some kinds' qualifier. It is a present-tense description of how LLMs were in 2023. It has no hedge.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary. He contrasts LLMs with calculators, so 'floating point' loosely means exact numeric calculation, and integer multi-digit multiplication is a fair test. Reading him as meaning tool-free LLMs fits the contrast he draws. The 2023 window up to the post date is reasonable.

evidence.note: A peer-reviewed 2023 study (v3 dated 2023-10-31, before the post). Off-the-shelf GPT-4 scored about 59% on 3x3-digit multiplication, far below a calculator. Integer tests are a fair stand-in under the contract.
Same paper, abstract. It explains how the models work (subgraph matching), not how well they do on pattern tasks. It is consistent with the claim's framing but does not measure 'great at'.

OpenAI's GPT-4 report gives human-level scores on professional and academic benchmarks, including the bar exam. This is a company disclosure, not an independent finding, but it backs the weak 'some kinds of pattern matching' half.

reviews.rationale: Both halves hold for 2023. Leading tool-free LLMs often got routine multi-digit multiplication wrong (e1: GPT-4 59% correct), and they did well on many pattern-heavy benchmarks (e3). GSM-8K at 92% with chain of thought involves simple numbers in word problems, and code tools fall outside the reading, so neither counts against him. Evidence was retrieved after the evaluation date, but every item was published in 2023, so it is usable.
